### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via KnowledgeSourceSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `415e75b690a42a360fb9938722477c59ede89ef8` — the merge of head `4d6fd4dca1237a18ddd20d54a996feb5681ac34b` into base `e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 415e75b690a42a360fb9938722477c59ede89ef8 && git checkout 415e75b690a42a360fb9938722477c59ede89ef8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa 4d6fd4dca1237a18ddd20d54a996feb5681ac34b && git checkout -B drift-repro e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa && git merge --no-ff 4d6fd4dca1237a18ddd20d54a996feb5681ac34b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4d6fd4dca1237a18ddd20d54a996feb5681ac34b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.knowledge-source-registration-governed.ts + none

Inputs read: card #38022 (body, amendment 7223636019, triage 7224179983, claim 7227517864, dev report 7228315278), PR #38050 (body, 5 files), the net diff of the head against merge base `e3bdc748841f8ec72aedc3d795227273f25c6baa`, and the check-runs on the head: 60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the generated-page point below was settled by reading the generator and comparing text.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged, and that is right. `knowledge_source.id` stays `retiredKey(...)`, which is `z.never().optional()`; only the guidance string grows. No key, value or requirement moves on `KnowledgeSourceSchema`.
- Public surface that does move, all of it text: (a) the refusal message a parse prints for `knowledge_source.id`; (b) the `[REMOVED]` description of that key in the emitted JSON schema, and from it the `id` row of `content/docs/references/ai/knowledge-source.mdx`; (c) the `reason` of the upgrade entry `knowledge-source-registration-governed`, which `os migrate meta --from 18` prints as a semantic notice. Each is right: an added qualification, nothing withdrawn.
- The entry's `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `acceptanceCriteria` and `conversionIds` are byte-identical to the merge base. Only `reason` changes.
- No export, type or committed baseline moves: the diff carries no `api-surface/`, `authorable-surface/`, `export-origins/` or manifest file, and the gates that would red on a stale one are green on this head.
- The generated page, judged as asked. `content/docs/references/ai/knowledge-source.mdx` was edited by hand, and its bytes equal what the generator emits. Read: `retiredKey` (`packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts:194`) describes the key as `[REMOVED] ` plus the guidance; `renderProperties` (`packages/spec/scripts/lib/schema-section.ts:539-546`) writes the row as key, type, required cell and the description passed through `escapeMdxDescription`, then backslash and pipe escaping. The new sentence holds no brace, angle bracket, pipe or backslash outside a code span, so the escape is the identity on it. Concatenating the head's string literals (the `id` block, `CODE_DOOR_18`, `MIGRATE_18`) under that rule gives a 972-character row equal, character for character, to line 54 of the page at the head. The gate that checks it is `check:docs` (`build-docs.ts --check`), step `check-generated-reference-docs-are-in-sync` of the unfiltered job `Type Check · source gates` in `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, rolled up by that job's `Lane verdict` step; that check-run concluded success on this head. The hand edit is therefore indistinguishable from a regeneration.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/knowledge-id-underscore-exception.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch. It matches what the diff publishes: prose in a published package, no change to what an author can write. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes patch (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3).
- Clause-②: no — stated on the PR body and in the changeset body, with no arm, and correct: nothing is widened or narrowed.
- The repo is in pre mode (`.changeset/pre.json`, tag `next`), so the patch folds into the next 19.0.0-next release. `Check Changeset` concluded success.
- The landed `.changeset/pre/37304-knowledge-source-governed-type.md` is left alone, as the card rules: it is consumed (its text is already in `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`), not pending.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, tests not run locally (`knowledge-source.test.ts`, `retired-key-migrate-sentence.test.ts`; verify lock never acquired): answered by the head's check-runs. `Test Core` and its ten shards concluded success on `4d6fd4dca1237a18ddd20d54a996feb5681ac34b`, which is the merge of main into the dev's commit `d60a6cef7d`, so the pins ran on the tree that would land. The tombstone still ends with `CODE_DOOR_18` then `MIGRATE_18`, the order the jsdoc and the sentence test require. No local run is owed.
- Dev flag, `gen:docs` and `check:generated` not measured: answered in ① above; the gate is green and the bytes agree with the generator as read.
- Dev flag, `check:docs-transcript-drift` exit 3 locally (prerequisite missing): it runs in `Type Check · workspace`, which concluded success.
- Published or pending, judged as asked. The entry file is on main and is also in a published pre-release: commit `3c53b854ac` (#38015), which wrote the sentence this PR qualifies, is an ancestor of tag `@objectstack/spec@19.0.0-next.2`, and npm serves that version under dist-tag `next`. It is in no stable version: `latest` is 18.6.0, and 19.0.0 is unreleased. So the edit does change text that a pre-release tarball already carries, but not an entry of a released major: the entry belongs to protocol 19, whose line is still open. Its identity (`id`, `surface`, `conversionIds`, acceptance criteria) is untouched, the change qualifies one sentence of `reason`, and the same entry's text was already revised once inside this line (#37676 shipped it in next.1, #38015 rewrote it for next.2). I found no rule in ADR-0087 or the migration sources that freezes an entry's prose before its major is released. The new changeset carries the correction into the next pre-release. Accepted.
- SQL push-down: no code path, query, id materialisation or join is added. Nothing to flag.
- The docs-drift advisory on the PR lists `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`, which this PR itself rewrites.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.knowledge-source-registration-governed.ts` (first item of the card amendment). The new sentence says an adapter whose store outlives the process keeps the index built under the old id, and the memory adapter holds nothing across a restart. Read against the live tree: `KnowledgeMemoryAdapter` keeps everything in a private `Map` (`packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/src/index.ts`, whose own doc says its index does not outlive the process); the Turso and pgvector adapters keep generation tables keyed by the source's name and drop them only in `dropSource`; `unregisterSource` leaves the index with its adapter and `dropMetadataSource` serves metadata items only. The sentence holds. The following sentences ("No source holds that key any more ...") still read correctly after the insertion, and the unchanged acceptance criterion ("the adapter holds nothing under the old id") stays satisfiable on every adapter, trivially on memory.

`packages/spec/src/ai/knowledge-source.zod.ts` (second item of the card amendment, plus the exception itself). The tombstone now says the index is found again except where the id began with an underscore, names why (`name` refuses it: `ROUTER_ADDRESSABLE_NAME_PATTERN` is `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/`), says the source is built again under a new name, names `dropSource`, and sends the reader to the entry, whose notices `os migrate meta` prints beside the rename (`conversionIds: ['knowledge-source-id-to-name']`; the CLI's word for them is "semantic notices"). It agrees with the entry sentence by sentence and no longer contradicts it. First consumer: an author whose 18 registration writes `id: '_x'` used to be told the index is found again and then met a refusal on `name` with no account of the orphaned index; the message now covers that case. Tried to break it: an adapter without `dropSource` (the member is optional in `knowledge-adapter.ts`) is covered by the entry's `replacement`, which the tombstone points at; the memory case is covered by the entry's new sentence.

N1 (nit) — the entry names Turso without condition among stores that outlive the process, yet the Turso store also accepts `:memory:` (`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/plugin.ts:30`, README option `url`), where nothing survives a restart either. The governing clause ("an adapter whose store outlives the process") is the condition and prescribes nothing false. Accepted deviation.
N2 (nit) — in the tombstone, "its old index is dropped with `dropSource`" is passive and can be read as something the platform does, and "after the conversion" names a conversion the message has not yet introduced (the `os migrate meta` sentence comes two sentences later). The entry it points to states the call and who makes it. Accepted deviation, or a follow-up card.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Outside this record's scope, for the lane seat's ACCEPT: the last sentence of the `id` row in `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` lists two subjects (an adapter without `dropSource`; a store that does not outlive the process) and then two outcomes in the opposite order. And, outside the diff, the summary of conversion `knowledge-source-id-to-name` still says no index is rebuilt, with no exception; a follow-up card could align it.
